stories.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
stories.reason: Google Project Zero's own head-to-head of a traditional fuzzer (Fuzzilli) against an AI agent (BigSleep/Gemini 3.6 flash) finding V8 bugs in production, six months of data, with a rediscovery experiment controlling for memorization. This is exactly the kind of primary, numeric, verifiable AI x cyber evaluation the profile wants -- running system, not a description of one.
key_facts: Apr-Sep 2026 production: Fuzzilli 316 total reports / 178 vulnerabilities; BigSleep 441 total / 95 vulnerabilities
Actionable vulnerabilities (deduped, fixed): BigSleep 45 vs Fuzzilli 37 -- roughly a tie
Overlap ~25% (20/81) of actionable reports; a separate experiment estimated ~60% overlap

Rediscovery test: BigSleep found ~62% of 112 historic Fuzzilli-found bugs from the introducing commit, a different bug for ~12% more, nothing on ~26%; follow-up prompting raised relevant-bug rate to ~70%
No significant memorization effect detected for pre-training-cutoff bugs
Overlap smaller for JIT-compiler bugs; bugs hard for the fuzzer tend to be hard for the agent too
Project Zero's conclusion: complementary, run both

stories.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
stories.reason: Schneier flags a real paper ('AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities') showing a cryptographic-locker backdoor can hide a dangerous capability inside a model's weights such that it survives fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient trigger search, and latent adversarial training -- i.e. elicitation-based safety audits can be made to fail in principle. Concrete PyTorch PoC, not just theory. This directly undercuts the premise of capability evals, which is squarely in the profile's eval-methodology lane.
key_facts: Backdoor = encrypted neural network embedded in host model weights via a 'digital locker' construction, unlocked only by a secret trigger
PoC in PyTorch; stand-in dangerous capability = chemical reaction prediction task (CBRN proxy)
Hidden capability survived fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training
Extends prior work (hiding fixed strings) to arbitrary computation
Commenters raised: can statistical tests detect the embedded network even if it can't be elicited; concern that releasing the PoC models helps attackers too

stories.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
stories.reason: Real, named PoC: researchers (Xint) smuggled encrypted chain-of-thought out of OpenAI's compaction feature by having the model echo it into the compacted item with space-for-tab substitution, which skipped the cross-model reasoning-reuse check because compaction runs on the same model. OpenAI confirmed and fixed it (Oct 23) and paid a $6,000 bounty -- primary source exists even though this article is secondary reporting.
key_facts: Technique: ask model to copy encrypted reasoning into compacted item, substitute tabs for spaces to dodge policy filters
Exploits a gap where OpenAI's cross-model reasoning-reuse check doesn't fire because compaction runs on the same model that produced the reasoning
Compacted item replayed through gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o, which emitted it as plaintext
Tested against gpt-5.6-sol only; GPT-6 Astra not checked
OpenAI fixed server-side Oct 23, 2026; paid Xint a $6,000 bounty
No confirmation the recovered text is a verbatim match, and no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation

stories.title: Retrieval's bottleneck is moving from finding to selecting
stories.reason: Concrete RAG-serving finding from Kapa.ai's own eval: the failure mode shifted from retrieval (finding) to selection -- 34% of gold chunks that search found were never shown to the agentic retriever. Matches 'how models are served' > 'how they are trained'. Single-company benchmark, not independently replicated, but numbers are specific and the mechanism is clearly explained.
key_facts: 18 months ago ~80% of failed eval cases were search misses; now roughly half are selection misses
34% of gold chunks found by search were never passed to the agentic retriever
Pipeline: retrieve 50 chunks, rerank up to 100 with Voyage-3, keep top 15; query decomposition via GPT-6 Luna
Moving top-5 to top-10 chunks raised gold-chunk coverage 14%, with falling precision
Retrieved chunks are ~2/3 of per-query cost in Kapa's assistants
Grep baseline matched deep-retriever recall but only 1-in-25 returned chunks were needed; deep retriever used 8x fewer tokens at ~6x precision

stories.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
stories.reason: Real law-enforcement case with primary sourcing (Seoul police via Yonhap): a named autonomous pentesting framework (ARTEX AI) used across 90+ breached South Korean orgs, 8.2M records, 38 extortion attempts at ~$270K each, 7 suspects identified / 1 arrested. Concrete numbers and a named tool, even though the AI-attribution and record count are police estimates, not independently verified.
key_facts: ARTEX AI: autonomous pentesting framework, also reportedly used against South Korean banks in a separate campaign
90+ orgs breached (schools, hospitals, companies, golf courses); ~8.2M records stolen (police estimate)
38 extortion incidents demanding 360M won (~$270,000) each not to leak data
7 suspects identified; leader (32, former pentester, worked security 2019-2022) arrested Oct 15, formally detained Oct 17, referred to prosecutors Oct 23; other 6 under investigation, not detained
Group allegedly switched from conventional tools to AI tooling in late Aug 2026

stories.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
stories.reason: OpenAI claims model-assisted results on three open problems (Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, QCD); 1112 points / 644 comments means the operator has already seen it -- surface briefly as a headline. Fetch was blocked (403), so this rides on the HN title/description alone; the scale of the claim (resolving ETH, a 20-year-old complexity conjecture) plus the size of the HN discussion suggests real but contested reception -- comments volume this high on a research claim usually means experts are pushing back.

stories.title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation attempts and remediation trends
stories.reason: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) is a large, concrete pure-cyber story -- Wiz's own telemetry: PHP runs on 65% of orgs in their dataset, exposure dropped sharply after disclosure, CISA added it to the KEV catalog off a honeypot's evidence. No AI angle, but the scale clears the 'needs to be large' bar for a cyber-only headline. Picking this as the primary source over the several duplicate write-ups of the same CVE pair.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, disclosed by Wiz Oct 21 2026; PHP <=7.3 lacks official backports
No fully-working public PoC found by Wiz; some partners privately shared working exploits
Strongest public evidence: Adel Karimi's honeypot, cited by CISA when adding it to the KEV catalog
Daily exposed-vulnerable-machine count fell ~67% over several days; PHP 7.3-or-earlier share of exposed machines fell from 8.3% to 5.7% in five days; significantly-affected orgs fell ~47.9%
One week post-disclosure, <53% of initially affected orgs remained vulnerable

stories.title: heterodoxin/AbliteratedOutTheBox
stories.reason: Running code, not a description: a llama.cpp fork that computes a refusal-direction vector at inference time (no weight edits) to suppress refusals, with a self-reported drop from 96.3% to 7.9% refusal on held-out harmful prompts. Fits the red-teaming-tooling line in the profile. Self-reported numbers and only 4 commits -- early and unverified, but it's a working artifact.
key_facts: Fork of llama.cpp; computes a 'refusal direction' and 'disclaimer direction' from contrastive activations, applies a projection edit at generation time
README claims refusal on held-out harmful prompts falls from 96.3% to 7.9% on Qwen3-8B, with the edit gate firing on 0.4% of benign prompts (self-reported)
155 stars, 16 forks, MIT license, only 4 commits on main -- early-stage
